question: What is a reverse proxy, and how is it different from a forward proxy?
answer_hinglish:
Reverse proxy ek server hota hai jo clients ke samne server ki tarah dikhta hai, lekin actual kaam peeche ke upstream server se karwata hai. Client ko pata hi nahi chalta ki peeche kitne servers hain. Forward proxy ulta hai: woh client ki taraf se kaam karta hai -- jaise office ka proxy jisse employees internet access karte hain, aur website ko office ka proxy dikhta hai, employee nahi.

Seedha yaad rakhne ka tarika: forward proxy client ko chhupata hai, reverse proxy server ko chhupata hai. Is project mein `createProxy()` reverse proxy hai: client hamare port 8080 se baat karta hai, aur hum request `UPSTREAM` (jaise http://127.0.0.1:3000) ko forward karte hain, response wapas bhej dete hain.

Interview mein bolo: reverse proxy ke upar hi load balancing, TLS termination, caching, compression aur rate limiting jaisi cheezein banti hain. Nginx, Caddy, HAProxy aur cloud load balancers sab isi category mein aate hain. H11 mein hum pehle sirf forwarding sahi karte hain, phir load balancing upar rakhenge.
why_needed: Ek jagah (entry point) chahiye jahan se saari traffic guzre, taaki security, routing aur scaling ek hi jagah ho sake.
real_world_analogy: Hotel ka reception: guest reception se baat karta hai, andar kaunsa staff kaam kar raha hai guest ko pata nahi. Forward proxy aise hai jaise ek secretary jo aapki taraf se baahar calls karti hai.
how_it_works: Client TCP connection hamare server se banata hai, hum HTTP request parse karte hain, ek naya request upstream ko bhejte hain, upstream ka response wapas stream karte hain. Client aur upstream ke beech do alag TCP connections hote hain.
in_this_project: src/proxy.ts mein createProxy() http.createServer ke andar handle() chalata hai, jo http.request se upstream ko call karta hai aur response ko pipe karta hai.
code_example:
const server = createProxy({ upstream: new URL("http://127.0.0.1:3000") });
server.listen(8080, "127.0.0.1");
advantages: Ek entry point: TLS, auth, rate limit ek jagah
Backend ko internet se chhupa sakte hain
Backend badalna client ko dikhta nahi
disadvantages: Ek extra hop: thodi latency aur ek aur cheez jo fail ho sakti hai
Agar proxy single instance hai toh woh khud single point of failure hai
common_mistakes: Forward aur reverse proxy ko mix karna
Sochna ki proxy sirf security ke liye hai, jabki scaling bhi uska kaam hai
follow_up_questions: Kya reverse proxy aur API gateway same cheez hain?
Client ke liye proxy ke peeche 1 server ho ya 10, kya fark padta hai?

question: What is the difference between a Layer 4 and a Layer 7 proxy, and which one is this?
answer_hinglish:
Layer 4 proxy sirf TCP bytes dekhta hai: kaun se IP aur port se connection aaya, aur woh bytes ko bina samjhe doosri taraf bhej deta hai. Layer 7 proxy HTTP samajhta hai: method, path, headers, status code. Isliye L7 proxy path ya Host header ke basis par routing kar sakta hai, headers add ya remove kar sakta hai, aur har request ko alag treat kar sakta hai.

Yeh project L7 proxy hai, kyunki hum `req.method`, `req.url` aur `req.headers` padhte hain, hop-by-hop headers hatate hain, X-Forwarded-For set karte hain, aur status code ke hisaab se 502 ya 504 return karte hain. L4 proxy yeh sab nahi kar sakta.

Trade-off: L4 tez aur sasta hai (parsing nahi) aur kisi bhi TCP protocol ke saath chalta hai (database, SMTP). L7 zyada flexible hai lekin har request parse karne ka CPU cost hai. Real systems mein aksar dono hote hain: L4 load balancer sabse upar, uske peeche L7 proxies.
why_needed: Sahi layer chunna design ka pehla decision hai: sirf bytes balance karne hain ya HTTP ke basis par decisions lene hain.
real_world_analogy: L4 post office ka sorting machine hai jo sirf pincode dekhta hai; L7 woh clerk hai jo chitthi kholke padhta hai aur uske hisaab se kaam karta hai.
how_it_works: L4 mein connection ke bytes bina interpret kiye copy hote hain (splice). L7 mein HTTP parser request ko headers aur body mein todta hai, aur proxy naya request banata hai.
in_this_project: createProxy http module use karta hai, jo HTTP parse karta hai, isliye hamari saari logic (headers, status mapping, Via) L7 hai.
advantages: L7 mein path/host/header based routing possible
Per-request retries, logging, error pages possible
disadvantages: Har request parse hoti hai: L4 se zyada CPU
Sirf HTTP ke liye (WebSocket ke liye extra kaam)
common_mistakes: Sochna ki L7 hamesha behtar hai
TLS termination ko L4 ka kaam samajhna
follow_up_questions: Database traffic ke liye L4 ya L7?
L7 proxy ke peeche WebSocket kaise chalega?

question: Why would you put a reverse proxy in front of an application?
answer_hinglish:
Teen-char bade reasons hain. Pehla, ek hi public entry: TLS certificate, rate limiting, logging ek jagah lagte hain, har app mein alag alag nahi. Doosra, scaling: peeche kitne bhi app instances ho sakte hain, proxy unke beech requests baant sakta hai (stage 2 mein hum yeh banayenge). Teesra, safety: app sirf 127.0.0.1 par listen kare toh internet se seedha reach nahi hota; sirf proxy dikhta hai.

Hamare deployment mein yahi hota hai: Oracle server par Caddy 80/443 par TLS handle karta hai, aur peeche apps 127.0.0.1 par chalti hain. Hamara proxy Caddy aur apps ke beech baith sakta hai, aur load balancing ya health checks jaisi cheezein add karega.

Dhyan rakho: proxy ek extra hop hai. Uski latency chhoti hoti hai, lekin proxy khud fail ho sakta hai, isliye production mein usko monitor aur restart karna padta hai (systemd ya Docker restart policy).
why_needed: Applications ko har baar TLS, logging, rate limit khud implement nahi karna padta, aur unko seedha internet se bachaya ja sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Mall ka main gate: security guard, parking aur directions ek jagah; andar ki dukaanein khud gate nahi sambhalti.
how_it_works: Client proxy se baat karta hai; proxy request ko dekhta hai (aur kuch change karta hai), phir upstream ko bhejta hai. Upstream sirf proxy ko jawab deta hai.
in_this_project: createProxy ek upstream ko forward karta hai, trustForwarded option Caddy jaise upar wale proxy ke saath kaam karne ke liye hai, aur index.ts default mein 127.0.0.1 par listen karta hai.
advantages: Cross-cutting concerns ek jagah
Backend ko directly expose nahi karna padta
Zero-downtime deploys aur scaling ka base
disadvantages: Extra hop, extra failure point
Misconfigured proxy poore site ko down kar sakta hai
common_mistakes: App ko 0.0.0.0 par expose chhod dena aur proxy bypass hone dena
Proxy ke peeche real client IP ko bhool jaana
follow_up_questions: Proxy ko highly available kaise banate hain?
Caddy ke hote hue apna proxy kyun?

question: What are hop-by-hop headers, and why must a proxy not forward them?
answer_hinglish:
HTTP headers do tarah ke hote hain. End-to-end headers (Content-Type, Authorization, Accept) message ke baare mein hain aur client se server tak jaane chahiye. Hop-by-hop headers sirf ek TCP connection ke baare mein hain: `Connection`, `Keep-Alive`, `Transfer-Encoding`, `TE`, `Trailer`, `Upgrade`, `Proxy-Authenticate`, `Proxy-Authorization`. Proxy ke liye client-wali connection aur upstream-wali connection do alag cheezein hain, toh in headers ko aage bhejna galat hai.

Example: client ne `Connection: close` bheja, matlab "yeh connection band kar dena". Agar hum yeh upstream ko forward kar dein, toh upstream apna connection band kar dega, jabki woh hamare aur uske beech ka mamla tha. Ya `Keep-Alive: timeout=5` -- yeh client-ke-saath ki baat hai.

Is project mein `stripHopByHop()` in headers ko hata deta hai. Test `does not forward hop-by-hop headers...` ek real request bhejta hai aur echo upstream se check karta hai ki `keep-alive` upstream tak nahi pahunchi.
why_needed: Agar proxy yeh headers forward kare toh connection management ke settings galat jagah lag jaate hain aur request smuggling jaise bugs ka darwaza khulta hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier: parcel (end-to-end) aage jaata hai, lekin 'is gaadi ko yahan roko' wali chit sirf us gaadi ke driver ke liye hoti hai.
how_it_works: RFC 9110 mein hop-by-hop headers ki list hai, plus Connection header mein jo bhi naam likhe hon woh bhi hop-by-hop maane jaate hain. Proxy dono ko hata deta hai aur apni connection ke liye khud decide karta hai.
in_this_project: headers.ts mein HOP_BY_HOP set hai aur stripHopByHop() ek naya object banata hai jisme woh keys nahi hoti. proxy.ts request aur response, dono taraf buildUpstreamHeaders aur buildClientHeaders ke andar isko use karta hai.
advantages: Connection-level settings leak nahi hoti
Smuggling jaise bugs ka surface kam
disadvantages: List maintain karni padti hai
Upgrade (WebSocket) strip karne se woh feature chalta nahi, alag handling chahiye
common_mistakes: Sirf Connection header hata dena, uske andar naam wale headers chhod dena
Response ke hop-by-hop headers ko bhoolna
follow_up_questions: Transfer-Encoding hop-by-hop hai toh chunked body ka kya hota hai?
WebSocket ke liye Upgrade ko kaise allow karoge?

question: Why does the proxy also remove headers that are only NAMED inside the Connection header?
answer_hinglish:
HTTP spec kehta hai ki `Connection` header mein jo bhi header naam likha ho woh bhi hop-by-hop hai. Misal: `Connection: keep-alive, X-Secret` ka matlab hai ki `X-Secret` bhi sirf is hop ke liye hai aur aage nahi jaana chahiye. Agar proxy sirf fixed list hataye, toh `X-Secret` upstream tak pahunch jata.

Yeh sirf theory nahi hai, security issue bhi hai: attacker `Connection: X-Auth-User` bhej kar proxy se woh header hatwa sakta hai jo proxy ne khud add kiya tha (jaise ek internal auth header), kyunki proxy ne usko hop-by-hop maan liya. Isliye jo bhi headers proxy khud lagata hai (X-Forwarded-For, Via) woh strip ke BAAD lagane chahiye -- is project mein `buildUpstreamHeaders` pehle strip karta hai, phir hi X-Forwarded-* aur Via set karta hai, toh attacker unko hata nahi sakta.

Test `does not forward hop-by-hop headers, including ones named in Connection` exactly yeh dikhata hai: `x-secret` upstream ke echo mein nahi aata, `x-keep` aata hai.
why_needed: Spec compliance aur ek real header-stripping attack se bachaav.
real_world_analogy: Chit par likha hai 'is gaadi ke saath X aur Y ko bhi mat bhejna': driver ko woh bhi roknaa padta hai, sirf standard list nahi.
how_it_works: stripHopByHop Connection ko comma se todta hai, har token ko lowercase karke ek set mein rakhta hai, aur un naamon wali headers bhi skip karta hai.
in_this_project: headers.ts::stripHopByHop mein `named` set bana ke check hota hai. buildUpstreamHeaders strip ke baad hi X-Forwarded-For aur Via set karta hai, isliye proxy ke apne headers safe rehte hain.
advantages: Spec ke saath sahi
Attacker proxy ke headers hatwa nahi sakta (agar order sahi ho)
disadvantages: Zyada code aur test
Case-insensitivity aur whitespace ka dhyan rakhna padta hai
common_mistakes: Proxy ke apne headers ko strip se pehle lagana
Case-sensitive comparison
follow_up_questions: Agar attacker Connection: Host bheje toh?
Header names HTTP/2 mein kaise alag hote hain?

question: What is X-Forwarded-For and why does the application behind a proxy need it?
answer_hinglish:
Proxy ke peeche ka app jab socket se remote address padhta hai, toh use hamesha proxy ka IP dikhta hai (jaise 127.0.0.1), asli client ka nahi. Isse per-IP rate limit, geo-location, audit logs aur abuse detection sab toot jaate hain. Isliye proxy `X-Forwarded-For` header add karta hai jisme asli client ka IP hota hai, aur app use padhti hai.

Agar request kai proxies se guzri ho, toh header ek chain banata hai: `client, proxy1, proxy2`. Har proxy apne se pehle wale hop ka IP (socket address) right side mein jodta hai.

Is project mein `buildUpstreamHeaders` socket ka `remoteAddress` leta hai, `normalizeIp` se `::ffff:10.1.2.3` jaise IPv4-mapped address ko `10.1.2.3` banata hai, aur yahi X-Forwarded-For mein daalta hai. Saath mein `X-Forwarded-Proto` aur `X-Forwarded-Host` bhi set hote hain, taaki app ko pata ho ki client ne http ya https aur kaunsa host use kiya tha.
why_needed: Bina iske backend ko asli client dikhta hi nahi, aur IP-based features (jaise P01 ka per-IP rate limiter) kaam nahi karte.
real_world_analogy: Receptionist visitor ka naam register mein likh deta hai, taaki andar ka staff ko pata ho ki asli visitor kaun hai, receptionist nahi.
how_it_works: Proxy upstream ke liye naya request banata hai, jisme X-Forwarded-For header mein client ka socket IP jodta hai. Backend leftmost value par naya trust nahi kar sakta -- sirf apne trusted proxies ke baad wali value.
in_this_project: headers.ts::buildUpstreamHeaders aur normalizeIp. Tests: ignores a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For by default; appends to the chain when the previous hop is trusted.
advantages: Asli client IP backend tak pahunchta hai
Proto/Host se redirect aur absolute URLs sahi bante hain
disadvantages: Header client bhi bhej sakta hai, isliye trust ka sawaal aata hai
Standard Forwarded header (RFC 7239) alag hai, dono formats chalte hain
common_mistakes: X-Forwarded-For ki leftmost value ko blindly maan lena
IPv4-mapped IPv6 address ko normalize na karna
follow_up_questions: X-Forwarded-For aur Forwarded header mein kya fark hai?
Backend kaise decide kare ki kitne proxies trusted hain?

question: Why does this proxy overwrite X-Forwarded-For by default instead of appending to it?
answer_hinglish:
X-Forwarded-For ek normal HTTP header hai, toh client kuch bhi bhej sakta hai -- jaise `X-Forwarded-For: 6.6.6.6`. Agar proxy usko blindly aage bhej de aur backend leftmost value pe bharosa kare, toh attacker apna IP chhupa sakta hai, ya per-IP rate limit bypass kar sakta hai (har request mein naya fake IP). Yahi cheez P01 rate limiter mein bhi dikhi thi: `RL_TRUST_FORWARDED_FOR` tabhi true hona chahiye jab app nginx ke peeche ho.

Isliye default behaviour: proxy client ka bheja hua X-Forwarded-For ignore karta hai aur socket ka real peer address likhta hai. Jab hamare upar ek trusted proxy (jaise Caddy) ho, tab `trustForwarded: true` set karte hain, aur tab hum chain extend karte hain: `198.51.100.7, 127.0.0.1`.

Test `overwrites a spoofed X-Forwarded-For by default` fake 6.6.6.6 bhejta hai aur upstream ko `127.0.0.1` milta hai. Maine yeh bhi check kiya ki agar condition ko tod dein (hamesha trust) toh yeh test fail hota hai.
why_needed: IP-based security (rate limits, bans, audit) tabhi kaam karti hai jab IP forge na ho sake.
real_world_analogy: Reception par ID check: visitor ke kehne se naam nahi likhte, ID card dekhke likhte hain.
how_it_works: Edge proxy ko socket address hi sach maanna chahiye. Chain tabhi extend karte hain jab pichla hop khud hamara trusted proxy ho, kyunki tab hi uski likhi value sach hai.
in_this_project: headers.ts::buildUpstreamHeaders mein `opts.trustForwarded && priorFor` ka branch; index.ts TRUST_FORWARDED env var se option set karta hai (default false).
advantages: Default safe hai: edge par spoofing nahi
Option se chained proxies bhi supported
disadvantages: trustForwarded galat jagah true kiya toh spoofing wapas aa jaati hai
Agar peeche koi aur proxy trusted hai par alag CIDR se, abhi per-IP trust list nahi hai
common_mistakes: Hamesha append karna
Public-facing edge par trustForwarded=true rakhna
follow_up_questions: Trusted proxies ki IP list se trust kaise karoge?
Cloudflare ke peeche asli client IP kaise milta hai?

question: How does the proxy detect a request loop, and what does it return?
answer_hinglish:
Agar galti se proxy ka `UPSTREAM` khud proxy hi ho (ya A -> B -> A jaisa chain ban jaye), toh request ghoomti rehti hai: har hop naya connection kholta hai jab tak sockets ya memory khatam na ho jayein. Yeh ek aasan misconfiguration hai aur poora server hila sakta hai.

Solution HTTP ka `Via` header hai. Har proxy, spec ke hisaab se, request par `Via: 1.1 <apna naam>` jodta hai. Hamara token `h11-proxy` hai. `hasLoop()` incoming Via ko comma se todta hai aur dekhta hai ki koi hop hamara token toh nahi. Agar haan, toh request pehle hi hamare se guzar chuki hai, aur hum 508 Loop Detected return karte hain bina upstream ko call kiye.

Test `returns 508 when the request has already passed through this proxy` isi ko check karta hai. Note: 508 asal mein WebDAV ka status code hai, lekin loops ke liye widely use hota hai.

Limitation: sirf tab kaam karta hai jab beech ke saare proxies Via preserve karein. Ek aur defence max-hops counter (`Max-Forwards`) hota, jo yahan implement nahi hai.
why_needed: Misconfiguration se poora server (aur upstream) overload hone se bachana.
real_world_analogy: Chitthi par har post office apni muhar lagata hai; agar apni hi muhar dobara dikhe toh pata chal jata hai ki chitthi ghoom rahi hai.
how_it_works: Request par Via append hota hai (buildUpstreamHeaders). Agle hop par wapas aane par hasLoop() token pehchan leta hai aur 508 deta hai.
in_this_project: headers.ts::hasLoop aur VIA_TOKEN; proxy.ts::handle sabse pehle hasLoop check karta hai aur plain(res, 508, ...) deta hai.
advantages: Sasta aur standard mechanism
Loop turant cut ho jata hai
disadvantages: Beech ka koi proxy Via hata de toh detection fail
Max-Forwards jaisa hop count nahi hai
common_mistakes: Loop detection ko request body padhne ke baad karna
Via ko strip kar dena
follow_up_questions: Max-Forwards header kaise kaam karta hai?
Via header ka privacy concern kya hai?

question: How does the proxy move request and response bodies, and why does memory stay flat for big files?
answer_hinglish:
Proxy body ko memory mein jama nahi karta. `req.pipe(up)` client ki request body ko seedha upstream request mein copy karta hai, aur `upRes.pipe(res)` upstream ke response ko seedha client mein. Node ke streams ke andar backpressure built-in hai: agar destination dheere hai (`write()` false return karta hai), toh source ko pause kar diya jata hai. Isse 2 GB ki file bhi chhote buffers se guzar jati hai, RAM 2 GB nahi khati.

Agar hum `await req.text()` jaisa kuch karte, toh poori body memory mein aati, aur 100 concurrent uploads se server out of memory ho sakta tha.

Tests mein 2 MiB upload aur 3 MiB download poori tarah sahi size mein pahunchte hain. Dhyan do: yeh tests sirf correctness (poore bytes aaye) dikhate hain. Memory flat rehti hai yeh maine measure nahi kiya; woh `pipe` ki design property hai, aur agar kabhi claim karna ho toh alag memory test se prove karna hoga.
why_needed: Proxy ko bade uploads/downloads par memory aur latency se bachana, aur first byte jaldi pahunchana.
real_world_analogy: Pipe mein paani: ek taraf se aata hai, doosri taraf se jaata hai, tanki mein jama nahi hota.
how_it_works: readable.pipe(writable) data events sunta hai, writable.write() ko call karta hai, aur jab write() false de toh readable ko pause karke 'drain' event ka intezaar karta hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: `req.pipe(up)` aur `upRes.pipe(res)`. Koi Buffer.concat ya body-parser nahi.
code_example:
req.pipe(up);          // client -> upstream
upRes.pipe(res);       // upstream -> client
advantages: Constant memory per request (design se)
First byte jaldi, kyunki buffering nahi
disadvantages: Body inspect ya modify karna mushkil (stream hai)
Retry karna mushkil: body pehle hi bhej di gayi hoti hai
common_mistakes: Poori body buffer karna
pipe ke error cases ko handle na karna
follow_up_questions: Agar aap response body ko modify karna chahein toh kya badlega?
Retry ke liye request body kaise save karoge?

question: Transfer-Encoding is hop-by-hop. So what does the proxy do with a chunked request body?
answer_hinglish:
Chunked encoding tab hoti hai jab sender ko body ki length pehle se pata nahi (jaise live upload). Client `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` bhejta hai. Yeh header hop-by-hop hai, isliye hum use strip karte hain. Lekin body ki length ab bhi nahi pata. Agar hum kuch na karein, toh upstream ko aisi body milegi jiski framing (kahan khatam hoti hai) undefined hai.

Isliye `buildUpstreamHeaders` mein: agar incoming request chunked thi, toh hum upstream ke liye `transfer-encoding: chunked` khud dobara set karte hain. Matlab proxy body ko re-frame karta hai -- client wali framing alag, upstream wali alag. Node ka ClientRequest phir chunks ko sahi format mein likhta hai.

Yeh khaas tab important hai jab method GET/DELETE jaisa ho kyunki Node tab by default chunked use nahi karta. Test `re-frames a chunked request body` do alag writes bhejta hai (`part-one,` aur `part-two`) bina Content-Length ke, aur upstream ko poori body `part-one,part-two` aur `transfer-encoding: chunked` milta hai.
why_needed: Length-less bodies ko bina corrupt kiye forward karna.
real_world_analogy: Do alag courier companies: pehli ke packing ka tarika doosri se alag ho sakta hai; beech ka agent maal nikalke apne tarike se pack karta hai.
how_it_works: HTTP/1.1 body framing do tarah ki hoti hai: Content-Length ya chunked. Proxy ek connection se body padhta hai (framing decode), aur doosri connection par apni framing se likhta hai.
in_this_project: headers.ts::buildUpstreamHeaders ke end mein chunked check. Test: re-frames a chunked request body (test/proxy.test.ts).
advantages: Streaming uploads bina length ke chalte hain
Dono connections ki framing independent
disadvantages: Request smuggling ka surface: Content-Length aur Transfer-Encoding dono aaye toh behaviour sahi hona zaroori (Node ka parser strict hai)
common_mistakes: Transfer-Encoding strip karke body ko bina framing ke bhej dena
Content-Length aur chunked dono set karna
follow_up_questions: HTTP request smuggling kya hai, aur proxy kaise bachta hai?
HTTP/2 mein chunked ka kya hota hai?

question: When does the proxy return 502 and when 504, and why does the difference matter?
answer_hinglish:
502 Bad Gateway matlab proxy ne upstream se valid jawab nahi paya -- connection refused, DNS fail, ya connection reset. 504 Gateway Timeout matlab upstream se connection to hua, lekin woh time par jawab nahi de paya. Client ya on-call engineer ke liye yeh farak bada hai: 502 mein upstream shayad down hai (process crash, galat port); 504 mein upstream zinda hai lekin slow ya hung hai (deadlock, DB slow query).

Is project mein `up.on("timeout")` ek `UpstreamTimeoutError` ke saath request destroy karta hai (idle timeout `upstreamTimeoutMs`, default 30 second). `up.on("error")` mein dekha jata hai: agar error `UpstreamTimeoutError` hai toh 504, warna 502. Test `returns 502 when the upstream refuses the connection` ek band port par jata hai, aur `returns 504 when the upstream does not answer in time` ek server banata hai jo kabhi jawab nahi deta, 150 ms timeout ke saath.

Zaroori baat: status code sirf tab badal sakte hain jab headers abhi bheje na gaye ho. Agar headers jaa chuke hain toh hum clean 5xx nahi bhej sakte (agla sawaal).
why_needed: Alag failure kinds ke liye alag signal, taaki debugging aur alerting sahi ho.
real_world_analogy: 502: aap ne phone kiya, number exist hi nahi karta. 504: phone uthaya par samne wala kuch bola hi nahi.
how_it_works: Node mein ECONNREFUSED, ENOTFOUND ya ECONNRESET error event deta hai; hang case mein socket timeout event aata hai jise hum khud error mein badalte hain.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: class UpstreamTimeoutError, up.on('timeout'), up.on('error') mein plain(res, 504 ya 502).
code_example:
if (err instanceof UpstreamTimeoutError) plain(res, 504, "Gateway Timeout");
else plain(res, 502, "Bad Gateway");
advantages: Debugging mein turant clue
Monitoring mein alag alert rules
disadvantages: Timeout idle-based hai, total request time ka limit nahi
Connect timeout aur response timeout alag nahi hain (abhi ek hi)
common_mistakes: Sab errors par 500 dena
Upstream ke apne 500 ko 502 bana dena
follow_up_questions: Upstream khud 500 de toh proxy kya kare?
Connect timeout aur read timeout alag kyun rakhte hain?

question: The upstream dies halfway through a response. What should the proxy do, and what does it do here?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh sabse tricky case hai. Proxy ne already `200 OK` aur headers client ko bhej diye. Ab upstream beech mein mar gaya. Ab hum status 502 mein nahi badal sakte, kyunki status line jaa chuki hai. Agar hum chup chap response end kar dein, toh client ko lagega ki download poora hua, jabki file adhoori hai -- silent corruption, sabse bura outcome.

Sahi tarika: client ki connection ko tod do, taaki client ko error mile (connection reset ya premature close). Is project mein `upRes.on("close")` mein check hota hai `if (!upRes.complete)`: agar upstream ka response complete nahi hua tha, toh `res.destroy()` call hota hai. Saath mein `aborted = true` set hota hai, aur log mein `aborted: true` aata hai.

Test `drops the client connection when the upstream dies mid-response` upstream se 1000 byte ka content-length ka waada karwata hai, 7 byte bhej ke socket tod deta hai; client ko status 200 dikhta hai lekin `res.text()` reject hota hai. Maine yeh bhi check kiya: `res.destroy()` hata dene par yeh test fail hota hai.
why_needed: Truncated response ko success samajhne se bachna.
real_world_analogy: Courier ne parcel ka aadha hi diya aur bol diya delivery complete: aap ko galat samajh aayega. Behtar hai ki woh saaf bole 'parcel adhoora hai'.
how_it_works: HTTP/1.1 mein Content-Length ya chunked terminator se body ka end pata chalta hai. Agar connection pehle toot jaye, toh IncomingMessage 'complete' false hota hai, aur 'close' event aata hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: up.on('response') ke andar upRes.on('close', ...) jo res.destroy() karta hai; up.on('error') mein bhi headersSent hone par res.destroy().
advantages: Client ko integrity failure dikhti hai
Log mein aborted flag se investigation aasan
disadvantages: Client ko generic network error milta hai, reason nahi
Retry sirf client kar sakta hai, proxy nahi (body pehle hi ja chuki)
common_mistakes: Response end() kar dena
pipe ke bharose rehna: pipe upstream error par destination ko end nahi karta ya destroy nahi karta
follow_up_questions: Kya proxy response ko retry kar sakta hai jab headers jaa chuke hon?
Range request ke saath resume kaise hota hai?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Option A: connection destroy karna (hamara). Option B: pehle poora response buffer karna taaki 502 de sakein -- lekin memory aur latency ka bada nuksan, streaming khatam. Hum A chunte hain kyunki proxy ka kaam streaming hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Upstream process kill, network cut, ya upstream ka OOM -- teeno mein upRes complete=false hota hai. Agar upstream chunked response bhej raha tha aur final 0-chunk nahi aaya, toh bhi incomplete maana jata hai.
advanced.alternatives: HTTP trailers ya response checksums se end-to-end integrity check; proxy ke saath range-based resume (client side); retry sirf tab jab abhi tak koi byte client ko na gayi ho.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada traffic par mid-stream failures bhi zyada honge; aborted flag ki rate ko metric banake alert lagana chahiye, taaki rolling deploys ke time pata chale.
advanced.production_improvements: Prometheus counter for aborted responses, upstream error type ke saath log, aur graceful drain deploys taaki in-flight responses poore ho jayein.

question: A client disconnects while the proxy is waiting for the upstream. Why must the proxy cancel the upstream request?
answer_hinglish:
Maan lo user ne bada report download shuru kiya aur tab band kar diya. Agar proxy upstream request chalta rehne de, toh upstream CPU, DB query aur bandwidth us response par kharch karta rahega jo koi padhne wala nahi. Zyada users ke saath yeh sockets aur workers khatam kar sakta hai.

Is project mein `res.on("close")` mein check hota hai: agar response `writableFinished` nahi hai (yaani client ke paas pura response nahi pahunchi), toh `up.destroy()` call hota hai. Is se upstream ko bhi connection close dikhta hai, aur woh apna kaam rok sakta hai (agar woh sahi likha hai).

Test `cancels the upstream request when the client disconnects` fetch ko AbortController se cancel karta hai, aur upstream ke `res.on("close")` ka intezaar karta hai. Maine yeh line hata ke bhi dekha: tab test timeout hota hai, matlab test sach mein is behaviour ko pakadta hai.

Dhyan: yeh tabhi kaam aata hai jab upstream khud disconnect ko sunta ho. Bahut se apps disconnect par bhi kaam chalate rehte hain.
why_needed: Resource waste aur socket leak rokna.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein customer chala gaya, par kitchen abhi bhi uska order bana raha hai. Waiter ko kitchen ko bolna chahiye 'order cancel'.
how_it_works: Client socket close hone par Node server 'close' event deta hai. Hum us event par upstream request ko destroy karte hain, jo uska socket band kar deta hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: res.on('close', () => { if (!res.writableFinished) up.destroy(); }).
advantages: Upstream ka wasted kaam kam
Sockets leak nahi hote
disadvantages: Upstream ko disconnect sunna aana chahiye, warna fayda nahi
Non-idempotent request (POST) beech mein cancel hone par upstream ka state unknown ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Sirf client ko response dena aur upstream ko chhod dena
Cancel ko finished response par bhi chalana
follow_up_questions: POST request cancel hone par kya hona chahiye?
Upstream ko kaise pata chale ki client chala gaya?

question: Why does the proxy use a keep-alive agent to the upstream, and what is maxSockets for?
answer_hinglish:
Naya TCP connection kholne mein ek round trip lagta hai (TCP handshake), aur agar TLS ho toh aur zyada. Agar har request par naya connection khole toh latency bhi badhegi aur server par bahut saare TIME_WAIT sockets bhi bante hain. Keep-alive agent connections ko pool mein rakhta hai aur agli requests dobara use karta hai.

`maxSockets: 256` ek safety limit hai: upstream ke saath ek saath kitne connections khule ho sakte hain. Isse upstream ko zyada concurrent load se bachate hain, aur jab limit cross hoti hai toh nayi requests queue mein intezaar karti hain. Default mein Node ka limit Infinity hota hai, jo upstream ko flood kar sakta hai.

Ek known risk (maine test nahi kiya): upstream apni idle connection ko ek timeout ke baad close kar deta hai (Node ka default keepAliveTimeout 5 second hai). Agar hum bilkul usi pal us connection par nayi request bhejein, toh ECONNRESET aa sakta hai. Isse bachne ke liye stage 3 mein idempotent requests ka retry aur agent ka timeout upstream se chhota rakhna planned hai.
why_needed: Latency kam karna aur connection churn rokna, saath hi upstream par concurrent load limit karna.
real_world_analogy: Taxi stand: har baar nayi taxi manga ke aane ka intezaar karne ki jagah, kuch taxis khadi rakhte hain.
how_it_works: http.Agent ek pool maintain karta hai host:port ke hisaab se. Request khatam hone par socket free pool mein jaata hai aur agli request ko mil jata hai, ya idle timeout par band hota hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: options.maxUpstreamSockets ?? 256 }); server close par agent.destroy().
code_example: const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: options.maxUpstreamSockets ?? 256 });
advantages: Kam latency, kam handshakes
Upstream par concurrent connections ki limit
disadvantages: Stale pooled connection par ECONNRESET ka risk
maxSockets chhota ho toh requests queue mein dher ho sakti hain
common_mistakes: Keep-alive band rakhna
maxSockets ko bahut bada ya infinite rakhna
follow_up_questions: Agar pool full ho toh requests ka kya hota hai?
Stale connection error ko kaise handle karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Bada pool = zyada concurrency lekin upstream par zyada load aur file descriptors; chhota pool = queueing. Number workload measure karke chunna chahiye, yahan 256 ek soch-samajh ke rakha gaya default hai, measured nahi.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Upstream restart: pooled sockets tootenge, agli requests par ECONNRESET ya EPIPE. Upstream slow: maxSockets full, queue badhti hai aur hamare timeout se 504 aate hain.
advanced.alternatives: Per-request naya connection (simple, slow); HTTP/2 ya multiplexing upstream ke saath (kam connections); undici ka Pool jo zyada tuning deta hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par per-upstream sockets zyada chahiye; 100x par multiple proxy processes ke har ek ka apna pool hota hai, toh total connections process count se multiply honge -- upstream ki limit dekhni padegi.
advanced.production_improvements: Pool metrics (active, queued sockets), idle timeout upstream ke keepAliveTimeout se kam, idempotent retry on ECONNRESET, aur connect timeout alag.

question: Should the proxy keep the client's Host header or rewrite it to the upstream's address?
answer_hinglish:
Do options hain. Pehla, Host preserve karna: upstream ko wahi Host milta hai jo client ne bheja (jaise `api.example.com`). Isse upstream virtual hosting, absolute URL generation aur redirects sahi bana sakta hai. Doosra, Host ko upstream ke address (`127.0.0.1:3000`) se badalna, jaisa nginx default mein karta hai: upstream ko lagta hai ki woh seedha baat kar raha hai.

Is project mein hum Host preserve karte hain, aur saath mein `X-Forwarded-Host` bhi dete hain. Wajah: hamara use case apps ke peeche proxy hai jahan app ko asli hostname chahiye (redirects aur cookies ke liye). Test `preserves the original Host header` upstream ko `127.0.0.1:<proxy port>` dikhata hai.

Trade-off: agar upstream Host ke basis par virtual host choose karta hai aur woh alag naam expect karta hai, toh preserve karna galat jawab de sakta hai. Us case ke liye ek `rewriteHost` option future mein add ho sakta hai. Abhi nahi hai, aur README ya code mein is par koi claim nahi hai.
why_needed: Redirects, cookies aur absolute URLs sahi domain par bane, aur upstream virtual hosts sahi chale.
real_world_analogy: Dak ka pata: letter par originally likha pata rakhna ya andar ke department ka pata likhna -- dono ke apne faide.
how_it_works: Host header HTTP/1.1 mein mandatory hai. Proxy use unchanged forward kare ya badal de, dono valid hain, bas upstream ke expectation ke saath match hona chahiye.
in_this_project: headers.ts::buildUpstreamHeaders Host ko touch nahi karta (stripHopByHop sirf hop-by-hop hatata hai) aur X-Forwarded-Host set karta hai.
advantages: Upstream asli hostname dekhta hai
Redirect aur cookie domains sahi
disadvantages: Host-based routing wale upstreams ke saath conflict possible
rewriteHost option abhi nahi hai
common_mistakes: Host ko bina soche rewrite karna aur redirects ka tootna
X-Forwarded-Host ko bina validate trust karna
follow_up_questions: Host header injection attack kya hai?
Multi-tenant app mein Host kaise use hota hai?

question: Why does createProxy reject https upstreams and upstream URLs with a path?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh ek jaan-boojh ke liye rakhi gayi simplicity hai. `https://` upstream ke liye TLS client, certificate verification aur SNI ka poora setup chahiye, jo ek alag badi cheez hai. Hamare deployment mein upstream apps same server par 127.0.0.1 pe chalti hain, toh plain http kaafi hai, aur TLS Caddy sambhalta hai.

Upstream URL mein path (jaise `http://host/base`) allow karne ke liye prefix rewriting chahiye (`/a` -> `/base/a`), query merge, trailing slash ke edge cases. Wo logic bugs ka source hai, isliye `createProxy` constructor mein hi `throw` kar deta hai, jaldi aur saaf error ke saath, bajaye ki chup chaap galat URL par request bheje.

Test `rejects upstreams it cannot honour` dono errors ko check karta hai. Fail-fast ka fayda: misconfiguration deploy ke waqt dikhti hai, production traffic aane par nahi. README mein 'Not implemented' section bhi yeh saaf likhta hai.
why_needed: Chhota, test-able scope rakhna, aur unsupported config ko chup chaap galat chalne se rokna.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant jo bolta hai 'hum home delivery nahi karte' bajaye ki aadha order bhej de.
how_it_works: Constructor URL object ko check karta hai: protocol 'http:' hona chahiye aur pathname '/' ho, search empty ho. Warna Error throw.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::createProxy ke shuru mein do if checks. Test: rejects upstreams it cannot honour.
code_example:
if (upstream.protocol !== "http:") throw new Error("only http:// upstreams are supported");
if (upstream.pathname !== "/" || upstream.search) throw new Error("upstream must not contain a path or query");
advantages: Fail-fast, config errors jaldi dikhte hain
Kam code, kam bugs
disadvantages: Remote https upstreams abhi supported nahi
Path-prefixed upstreams ke liye alag proxy ya rewrite chahiye
common_mistakes: Unsupported input ko ignore karke aage badh jaana
Documentation mein limitation na likhna
follow_up_questions: https upstream add karna ho toh kya badlega?
Path rewriting mein kaunse edge cases aate hain?

question: Walk through what handle() does for one request, in order.
answer_hinglish:
Pehle ek close listener lagta hai jo request khatam hone par log entry likhta hai (method, url, status, aborted, ms). Phir `hasLoop()` check: Via mein hamara token mila toh 508 aur return, upstream ko call nahi.

Phir `http.request()` banti hai: shared agent, upstream ka host aur port, method wahi, path `req.url` (path + query jaisa client ne bheja), headers `buildUpstreamHeaders` se (hop-by-hop strip, X-Forwarded-*, Via), aur `timeout`. Uske baad handlers: `timeout` par request ko UpstreamTimeoutError ke saath destroy; `response` par status aur filtered headers client ko likhna aur `upRes.pipe(res)` plus incomplete-body check; `error` par 502/504 ya (agar headers ja chuke) connection destroy. Aakhir mein `res.on('close')` upstream cancel ke liye, aur `req.pipe(up)` jo client body ko upstream mein stream karta hai.

Order important hai: handlers pehle lagte hain, pipe aakhir mein, taaki koi event miss na ho. Yeh function ~70 lines ka hai, aur isi mein proxy ka sara behaviour hai.
why_needed: Interview mein code explain karna aana chahiye, sirf concepts nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek sorting centre ka pura flow: parcel aaya, check hua, aage gaya, rasta kharab hua toh kya kiya.
how_it_works: Node ke event-driven model mein har step ek event handler hai: request, response, error, timeout, close.
in_this_project: proxy.ts::createProxy ke andar function handle(req, res).
advantages: Chhota aur padhne layak function
Har failure path ka apna handler
disadvantages: Ek function mein kaafi responsibilities; stage 2 mein upstream selection alag karna padega
common_mistakes: pipe pehle laga dena aur handlers baad mein
error handler mein headersSent check bhoolna
follow_up_questions: Stage 2 mein upstream selection kahan jodoge?
Handler ka order kyun matter karta hai?

question: Users say large downloads are truncated, but the proxy logs show status 200. How do you investigate?
answer_hinglish:
Symptom: client ko incomplete file milti hai, lekin log mein `status: 200`. Pehla shak: status line pehle hi chali gayi thi, aur baad mein upstream beech mein toota. Proxy ke log entry mein `aborted` field hai: `{"status":200,"aborted":true}` ka matlab hai ki response complete nahi hua. Isliye pehle logs mein `aborted: true` filter karo.

Agle steps: dekho kaunsa url aur kitni `ms` ke baad toota. Agar ek hi upstream instance ke saath hota hai toh upstream ke logs ya OOM kill (`dmesg`, `journalctl`) dekho. Agar sab files par ek hi time par hota hai toh deploy ya restart ka waqt (rolling restart mein in-flight responses kat jaate hain). Agar client side `aborted` hai (user ne cancel kiya), toh yeh normal hai, isliye pehle dekhna ki `aborted` kaun sa case hai.

Fix depends on cause: upstream memory leak/crash, ya graceful drain na hona, ya idle timeout bahut kam (UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS) jo slow downloads ko kaat raha ho.
why_needed: Mid-stream failures sabse mushkil dikhte hain kyunki status 200 hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Courier ne kaha 'delivered' (200), par dabbe mein aadha saman: pehle delivery slip nahi, packing dekhni padegi.
how_it_works: Hum res.statusCode log karte hain jo headers likhne ke time ka status hota hai, aur `aborted` flag res close par `!res.writableFinished` ya mid-stream upstream failure se set hota hai.
in_this_project: proxy.ts: res.on('close') mein log entry {status, aborted, ms}; upRes close aur up error dono aborted=true set karte hain.
advantages: Ek field se mid-stream failures pakad mein aate hain
disadvantages: aborted client-cancel aur upstream-failure dono mein true ho sakta hai; alag reason field abhi nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sirf status code par bharosa karna
Rolling restart ko cause ke roop mein na dekhna
follow_up_questions: aborted ko client-cancel aur upstream-failure mein kaise alag karoge?
UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT_MS kam hone se kya symptoms aate hain?

question: How does the proxy shut down gracefully on SIGTERM, and why does that matter for deploys?
answer_hinglish:
Deploy ya restart par process ko SIGTERM milta hai. Agar hum turant exit kar dein, toh jo requests abhi chal rahi hain (downloads, uploads) beech mein kat jaati hain, aur users ko errors dikhte hain. Graceful shutdown ka matlab: naye connections lena band, chalu requests ko poora hone dena, phir exit.

`src/index.ts::shutdown` yeh karta hai: `server.close()` naye connections rokta hai aur jab saare connections khatam ho jayein tab callback chalta hai (process.exit(0)). `server.closeIdleConnections()` un keep-alive connections ko turant band kar deta hai jo idle hain (warna woh close ko rok sakte hain). Aakhir mein ek 10 second ka safety timer hai: agar kuch requests phir bhi atki hain, toh process.exit(1) force-exit karta hai, taaki deploy hamesha ke liye na atke. Timer `unref()` hai taaki woh khud process ko zinda na rakhe.

Dhyan rakho: yeh tabhi poora kaam karta hai jab load balancer ya Caddy shutdown se pehle is instance ko rotation se nikaal de. Yeh stage 3 ke health checks ke saath achha judega. Honest note: is shutdown flow ka na koi automated test hai, na maine ise manually verify kiya hai. Pehle test likhna chahiye, tabhi ise 'working' bolna sahi hoga.
why_needed: Zero (ya kam) dropped requests rolling deploys par.
real_world_analogy: Dukaan band karne se pehle: naye customer lena band, jo andar hain unka bill banane do, phir shutter girao.
how_it_works: Node server.close() listening socket band karta hai aur existing connections ke khatam hone ka intezaar karta hai; closeIdleConnections() un sockets ko band karta hai jin par koi active request nahi.
in_this_project: index.ts::shutdown, SIGTERM aur SIGINT handlers.
advantages: Deploys par in-flight requests nahi katti (design se)
Force-exit timer se deploy atakta nahi
disadvantages: Is flow ka koi test abhi nahi hai
Load balancer ko drain ka signal chahiye warna naye requests aate rahenge
common_mistakes: Seedha process.exit karna
Idle keep-alive connections ko close na karna aur server.close ka atak jaana
follow_up_questions: Kubernetes mein preStop hook aur readiness ka rol kya hai?
10 second timeout kaise decide karoge?

question: Write a test that proves the proxy passes a redirect through to the client instead of following it.
answer_hinglish:
Proxy ka kaam redirect ko follow karna nahi hai; use client tak pahunchana hai. Agar proxy khud 302 follow karne lage, toh client ko location header kabhi dikhega nahi, aur cookies/URLs galat jagah jaayenge. Hamara code http.request use karta hai, jo redirects follow nahi karta, lekin test ke bina yeh ek assumption hi hai.

Test ka plan: ek chhota upstream banao jo `302 Location: /login` deta hai; proxy uske aage start karo; client side par `fetch(..., { redirect: "manual" })` use karo, taaki fetch bhi follow na kare; phir assert karo ki status 302 hai aur `location` header `/login` hai.

Yeh exactly wahi test hai jo `test/proxy.test.ts` mein `passes a redirect through to the client instead of following it` naam se hai, aur pass hota hai. `redirect: "manual"` zaroori hai: warna test fetch ke follow karne se galat green ho jata.
why_needed: Proxy ke behaviour ko ek assumption se test-backed fact banana.
real_world_analogy: Postman: chitthi par 'is naye pate par jao' likha hai, woh khud nahi jaata, receiver ko batata hai.
how_it_works: http.request redirect follow nahi karta. Hum status aur headers (Location) ko as-is client tak likhte hain.
in_this_project: test/proxy.test.ts mein yeh test hai aur baaki tests ke saath pass hota hai.
advantages: Chhota, deterministic test
Ek assumption ko pakka karta hai
disadvantages: Absolute Location URLs (upstream ke address wale) rewrite hone ka alag case hai, yahan test nahi hai
common_mistakes: fetch ko redirect follow karne dena
Upstream ka Location header 127.0.0.1:3000 wale URL se aaye toh uska rewrite expect karna
follow_up_questions: Absolute Location ko upstream ke address se proxy ke address mein kaise badloge?
Set-Cookie ke Domain/Path ko rewrite karne ki zarurat kab padti hai?

question: Where would this proxy sit relative to Caddy and the apps on the Oracle servers, and how are trust and TLS handled?
answer_hinglish:
Plan yeh hai (stage 4): internet -> Caddy (80/443, TLS, automatic certificates) -> hamara proxy (127.0.0.1:8080) -> apps (127.0.0.1:3000, 8000 etc., alag server par bhi ho sakti hain). Caddy TLS terminate karta hai, isliye hamare proxy ko https nahi samajhna padta. Proxy aur apps ke beech plain http chalta hai.

Trust ka sawaal: Caddy ke peeche hone par `TRUST_FORWARDED=true` hona chahiye, taaki Caddy ka bheja X-Forwarded-For aur X-Forwarded-Proto: https bach jaye. Lekin tab proxy ko 127.0.0.1 par hi listen karna chahiye, public interface par nahi, warna koi bhi bahar se fake X-Forwarded-For bhej sakta hai. Yeh dono settings saath chalni chahiye, aur index.ts mein HOST ka default 127.0.0.1 isi liye hai.

Network layout: A2 par proxy aur A1 par apps ho sakte hain, lekin tab traffic servers ke beech jaata hai, toh Oracle security list ko un ports ko sirf doosre server ke IP ke liye kholna padega (sab ko nahi). Abhi yeh deploy nahi hua hai; yeh design hai, aur stage 4 ke baad hi measure karke likhunga ki kaisa chalta hai.
why_needed: TLS, trust boundary aur network exposure ek saath sochne padte hain, warna ek galat default poori security tod deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Teen darwaze: bahar wala guard ID dekhta hai (Caddy), beech wala guard rasta batata hai (proxy), andar kamre (apps).
how_it_works: TLS Caddy par khatam hota hai; uske baad X-Forwarded-Proto: https header se app ko pata chalta hai ki client ne https use kiya. Trust boundary: sirf Caddy proxy se baat kar sakta hai, jab proxy loopback par listen karta hai.
in_this_project: index.ts: HOST default 127.0.0.1, TRUST_FORWARDED env, createProxy trustForwarded option. Deployment details: deployment/06-oracle-micro-server.md aur deployment/README.md.
code_example:
# systemd environment for the proxy behind Caddy
UPSTREAM=http://127.0.0.1:3000
HOST=127.0.0.1
PORT=8080
TRUST_FORWARDED=true
advantages: Caddy certificates sambhalta hai, hum sirf routing
Loopback par listen: bahar se bypass nahi
disadvantages: Ek aur hop aur ek aur process monitor karne ko
Servers ke beech plain http: private network par hi theek hai
common_mistakes: TRUST_FORWARDED=true ke saath proxy ko 0.0.0.0 par listen karwana
Server ke beech ports poori internet ke liye kholna
follow_up_questions: Kya apna proxy Caddy ko replace kar sakta hai? Kab nahi?
Zero-downtime deploy kaise hoga is layout ke saath?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Caddy ke sirf reverse_proxy se load balancing mil jaati hai, toh apna proxy sirf seekhne aur custom behaviour (stage 2 and 3) ke liye hai. Production mein battle-tested Caddy hi sahi hai jab tak apne proxy ke tests aur measurements na hon.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Proxy crash: systemd restart; Caddy ko 502 milega jab tak restart na ho. Caddy crash: poori site down. A2 server down: A1 ke apps alive par unreachable.
advanced.alternatives: Sirf Caddy ke upstream lists aur health checks; nginx upstream; HAProxy L4/L7; cloud load balancer.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x par ek proxy process CPU-bound ho sakta hai (single thread), toh multiple processes ya cluster; 100x par DNS ya L4 load balancer proxies ke upar.
advanced.production_improvements: Health checks (stage 3), metrics, rate limiting, mTLS ya private network between servers, aur measured capacity numbers stage 4 ke baad.

question: What limits the throughput of this proxy, and how would you scale it? (No benchmark numbers are claimed yet.)
answer_hinglish:
Node ek hi thread mein event loop chalata hai, toh ek proxy process ek CPU core tak seemit hai. Kaam ka bada hissa I/O hai (sockets), jo event loop ke liye sasta hai, lekin har request par HTTP parsing, header copy aur logging CPU leti hai. Streaming ki wajah se memory body size ke saath nahi badhti, lekin per-connection overhead rehta hai.

Scaling ke raaste: pehle ek server par multiple processes (Node `cluster` ya systemd ke multiple instances alag ports par) aur unke aage L4 distribution; phir multiple servers ke aage DNS ya cloud load balancer. Bottleneck pehle dhoondhna: CPU (profiler), socket limits (`ulimit -n`, maxSockets), ya upstream khud.

Honest baat: maine is project ke liye abhi koi throughput ya latency number measure nahi kiya, isliye koi nahi bol raha. Stage 4 mein k6 ya autocannon se Oracle server par load test karke numbers likhunga, aur tab hi README mein dalunga. Is ke bina 'X requests per second' bolna interview mein galat hoga.
why_needed: Capacity planning measurement se hoti hai, andaze se nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter wala cashier: uski speed seemit hai; zyada log aayein toh counters badhao, ya lines banao.
how_it_works: Event loop ek time par ek callback chalata hai. CPU-heavy kaam (parsing, JSON logging) loop ko block karta hai; I/O waiting nahi karta. Isliye per-core ek process chalana scaling ka pehla step hai.
in_this_project: Abhi single process: src/index.ts. Logging ek console.log JSON line per request hai (stdout synchronous ho sakta hai, jaise P01 mein ek real bug mila tha). Koi load test abhi nahi hai.
advantages: Simple design, reasoning aasan
Streaming se memory per request kam
disadvantages: Single thread: ek core limit
console.log stdout par chalta hai, tez load par slow ho sakta hai
common_mistakes: Bina measure kiye numbers bolna
Sirf proxy ko dosh dena jab upstream hi bottleneck ho
follow_up_questions: Cluster module kaise kaam karta hai aur sockets kaise share karta hai?
Event loop lag ko kaise measure karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Multiple processes throughput badhate hain, lekin har process ka apna pool, apne counters (least-connections stage 2 mein per-process hoga, global nahi) aur apni health state hoti hai. Shared state ke liye coordination chahiye.

advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x: per-core processes. 100x: multiple servers ke aage L4/DNS; upstream autoscaling; connection reuse (HTTP/2) upstream ke saath.
advanced.production_improvements: Async logging (P01 ka QueueHandler sabak), event-loop lag metric, ulimit tuning, load test results ko docs mein, alerts on 5xx and aborted.
